title: Pre-Market — Monday, Nov 9, 2026
html:
Oil slips, Delta gaps over its trigger, and Nvidia stumbles on a CEO scandal. Here's what I'm seeing before the bell. A quiet-looking Monday with a loud one coming: CPI is tomorrow at 8:30, so today is about patience.

The one thing

SPY is at $740.30 pre-market, up 0.7% but still under the $745 line. DAL has already jumped over your $88 trigger to $90.02, straight into the $91.86 target zone.

Triggers are decided at the intraday check, not in pre-market. With CPI tomorrow, the smart move is to let DAL prove it can hold above $88–89.92 during the day instead of chasing the open. Nvidia's 5.9% drop is a headline shock, not a change in your plan.

Overnight in plain words

  • Futures: S&P 500 about +0.6%, Nasdaq 100 about +0.4%, Dow about +1%. Nvidia's drop is the drag on the Nasdaq.
  • Asia and Europe: Japan's Nikkei and Korea's Kospi rose more than 1%, Hong Kong a little. Asian chip stocks gained despite the Nvidia news. Europe opened flat and later edged up (Stoxx 600 about +0.6%).
  • Oil: Brent about $97, WTI about $90, both down 1–2%. Trump said new strikes on Iran are "highly unlikely" while talks progress, even as ship attacks near Hormuz continue. Brent already fell 16% last week. Cheaper fuel is why airlines and cruise lines are up.
  • Rates and fear: 10-year yield 4.86% (little changed). The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is down about 9% to 23.3. Futures still price about 80% odds of a December rate hike.
  • Big headline: Nvidia's board opened an independent review after CEO Jensen Huang disclosed a relationship with a woman U.S. officials suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. The board says it has no sign secrets were compromised and backs him; House committee chairs asked for a briefing on Nov 18. NVDA is −5.9% pre-market.

SPY at the open

Pre-market: $740.30

  • Oct 6 record high: $781.62
  • Ceiling · 61.8% + 20- & 50-day: $763–765
  • 38.2–50% of the Oct–Nov drop: $751–757
  • The line · old floor, now ceiling: $744–745
  • PRE-MARKET: $740.30
  • Shelf · Nov 5 low + 1.382 ext: $732.50
  • Big floor · 200-day + 38.2% of run: $722–728
  • 50% of the Mar–Oct run: $703.87
  • If SPY opens above $745… it's the first step back over the old floor, but the SPY call waits until after CPI. Watch whether it holds into intraday; no SPY trade today.
  • If it holds between $732.50 and $745… that's the normal pre-CPI chop. Only names with their own trigger (DAL, PLTR) count, one contract at most.
  • If it opens below $732.50… Friday's bounce has failed and the $722–728 floor is next. No new longs; cash is a position.

Today's calendar

  • Today: No big data. Around 11:00 a.m.: NY Fed consumer inflation expectations (last 3.9%). 11:30 a.m.: 3- and 6-month bill auctions. 1:00 p.m.: 3-year note auction. 12:15 p.m.: Richmond Fed President Barkin speaks.
  • Earnings: After the close: Rocket Lab, Take-Two, Trump Media. Also on today's list: Constellation Energy, KKR, Occidental, The Trade Desk, Hims & Hers. No watchlist name reports today, so no IV-crush risk tonight.
  • Tomorrow: CPI at 8:30 a.m. Forecast +0.3% for the month (3.9% a year), core +0.2% (2.8% a year). CoreWeave reports after the close. Fed's Logan, Schmid and Bowman speak.
  • Ahead: NVDA earnings Nov 17, DELL Nov 24. Anyone holding those names' options through the report risks IV crush, the drop in option prices once the news is out.

Plays check (Options Playbook)

  • DAL Dec 18 $85 call · OPEN: Still valid. IV 44% vs moves 35% → FAIR. OI 5,101 · vol 81 · bid/ask $6.35/$6.75 (Friday). Entry ~$440, Friday mark $655. With DAL near $90 it's worth about $840 by my estimate (verify in Webull). Exit: a close below $83. $91.86 is target 1, the place to decide on taking the win.
  • DAL Dec 18 $90 call · WATCHING: Closer to triggering. IV 42% vs moves 35% → FAIR. OI 3,305 · vol 191 · bid/ask $3.95/$4.15 (Friday). Trigger: above $88 at the intraday check. Pre-market says yes, but it is a gap into resistance. Expect it to cost about $530 now (estimate, verify). One contract only before CPI. Exit below $83; targets $91.86, $95.18.
  • PLTR Dec 18 $175 call · WATCHING: Wait. IV 52% vs moves 50% → FAIR. OI 2,917 · vol 831 · bid/ask $6.05/$6.30 (Friday). At $159.95, inside the $153–160 zone but under $160. Needs above $160 intraday, or above $172.23. Off below $147.08.
  • BA Dec 18 $170 put · WATCHING: Wait. IV 33% vs moves 36% → FAIR. OI 4,123 · vol 127 · bid/ask $5.65/$6.10 (Friday). Moving away from the $165 trigger. The other entry is a rally that fails at $179–181.5. Exit above $185.
  • SPY Dec 18 $765 call · WATCHING: Off for today. IV 16% vs moves 14% → FAIR. OI 15,249 · vol 979 · bid/ask $6.28/$6.39 (Friday). The rule says above $745 at the check and only after Tuesday's CPI. Back on the table tomorrow.
  • Also open: HLT Dec 18 $380 call (HLT $376.15 pre-market on just 83 shares). Exit rule a close below $359.41 is far away. IV 26% vs moves 23% → FAIR; OI 281, bid/ask $9.30/$11.20, too thin for new money.

Alerts for today

  • DAL — price crosses above $91.86 → target 1 for the open $85 call; decide on taking the win
  • DAL — price crosses below $88.00 → the gap is failing; the $90 call trigger is off for now (below $83.00 → exit the $85 call)
  • PLTR — price crosses above $160.00 → the $175 call setup is live; the intraday check confirms (below $147.08 → idea off)
  • BA — price crosses below $165.00 → put trigger; the intraday check confirms
  • SPY — price crosses below $732.50 → Friday's bounce failed; no new longs, $722–728 is next

An alert means look now, not buy now. The intraday check confirms. Keep the HLT alert below $359.41 as it is.

Opening rule of the day

Don't chase a gap into resistance. DAL gapped over its trigger and straight toward its first target. Let the first 30 minutes settle. If it is still above $89.92 (the Nov 5 high) after 10:00, the breakout is real. If it slips back under $88, the gap was just oil-headline excitement. Either way, use a limit order at the mid: Friday's DAL spreads were 20–40 cents wide.

Sources: Webull pre-market snapshots and option quotes; Yahoo Finance: Stock market today, Nov 9; Yahoo Finance: Oil prices decline as Trump signals restraint on Iran; Nation Thailand: Brent falls on Nov 9; Yahoo Finance: European equities flatline as markets digest Nvidia board probe; Benzinga via Webull: Nvidia, AMD and SpaceX news.

Education, not personalized investment advice. Claude never places trades; check every quote in Webull before acting.
